also: of the greatest importance to me

terms.gloss: it is important, it matters a great deal
terms.grammar: impersonal verb (intersum); to whom, meā, tuā or a genitive; how much, magnī, plūris, maximē, nihil
evidence: Cic. Att. 11.22.2: illud meā magnī interest tē ut videam
Cic. Fam. 16.4.4: tuā et meā maximē interest tē valēre
Traupman 101: magnī (maximē) meā interest; permagnī meā interest
terms.comment: Latin says “X is important” as “X matters”: the thing that matters is the subject, as a clause (infinitive, ut, or a question) or a neuter pronoun; nihil interest, “it makes no difference”. Traupman gives magnus for the adjective and id magnī aestimāre, “to consider it important” (p. 332).

evidence: Phaedr. 1.15: quid rēfert meā cui serviam, “what does it matter to me whom I serve”
terms.comment: Frequent in comedy, rare in Cicero, who says interest (Lewis & Short). Quid rēfert? “What does it matter?”

terms.grammar: genitive of quality: rēs magnī mōmentī
evidence: Cic. Vatin. 19: maximī mōmentī et ponderis (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Off. 1.103: cum gravibus sēriīsque rēbus satis fēcerimus
M-O s.v. important (marked as a modern word; Trappen 1843)
terms.comment: Its only ancient use (Ps.-Quint. Decl. 13.12) means “momentary, quick”; magnī mōmentī says “important” classically.

phrases.latin: illud meā magnī interest tē ut videam
phrases.english: it matters a great deal to me to see you

phrases.latin: tuā et meā maximē interest tē valēre
phrases.english: it matters above all, to you and to me, that you get well

phrases.latin: quōmodo fābula, sīc vīta: nōn quam diū, sed quam bene ācta sit, rēfert
phrases.english: life is like a play: what matters is not how long it runs, but how well it is acted
